title: Concurrent POST /orders oversells: stock check and decrement are not atomic
description:
What happens: 10 concurrent POST /orders {productId:"p1",qty:1} are all accepted (201) against a stock of 2. Final stock is 1 (not 0 or negative), and only one unit is deducted while 10 units are promised. The single-threaded case correctly returns 409 "insufficient stock" once stock is exhausted, so the bound is intended but lost under concurrency. Repro: run `node .prelude/work/oversell-probe.mjs` — it resets p1 to stock 2, fires 10 concurrent orders of qty 1 (3 rounds), and checks the invariant successes*qty <= initialStock and initialStock-finalStock === successes*qty. Every round: 201:10, finalStock=1, acceptedQty=10, stockDelta=1.

Expected: POST /orders must not accept more units than available stock. Basis: /openapi.json POST /orders says "Place an order. Stock is decremented by qty; stock never goes below zero." and declares 409 "Insufficient stock"; the single-threaded path does return 409. Invariant: for a non-cancelled order the stock must be decremented by exactly qty, so initialStock - finalStock must equal the total accepted qty, and accepted qty must be <= initialStock.

Variants of the same root cause: qty=3 with stock 5 and 8 concurrent requests accepted 24 units (all 201); the decrement is not atomic (read-modify-write), so the last write wins.

review.reason: 脚本的不变量有文档依据（/openapi.json POST /orders 声明 "Stock is decremented by qty; stock never goes below zero" 并定义 409 Insufficient stock；/reset 文档确认 stock 覆盖语义，initial=2 由服务端实际返回）。断言不过弱：正确实现返回 201:2/409:8/stockDelta:2 即可 exit 0。脚本无语法或依赖问题，reset 失败与异常分支均 exit 0，本次走正常路径退出 1，不存在“环境/脚本自身失败”。输出 201:10、finalStock=1、acceptedQty=10、stockDelta=1 与描述完全一致，且 3 次重跑 3 次复现，并有 qty=3/库存5/并发8 接受 24 单位的同根因变体，独立笔记也记录了先读后写的非原子扣减，证据充分证明并发下单超卖。

title: Concurrent coupon claim exceeds quota (remaining never decremented atomically)
description:
What happens: with coupon SAVE10 (quota 5, remaining 5), 15 concurrent POST /coupons/SAVE10/claim all return 201; remaining ends at 4. The quota of 5 is exceeded threefold, and remaining is not even decremented once per claim (15 claims -> -1 decrement). Sequentially the service does enforce the quota and returns 409 "Quota exhausted" once remaining hits 0.

Expected: at most `remaining` claims may succeed, and remaining must never go below zero. Basis: /openapi.json POST /coupons/{code}/claim says "Claim one use of a coupon. remaining never goes below zero." and declares 409 "Quota exhausted". Invariant: successes <= initial remaining; final remaining == initial remaining - successes.

Same root cause as f-001 (non-atomic check-then-decrement) but on a different endpoint/resource, so it needs a separate fix. Repro: `node .prelude/work/coupon-probe.mjs` -> 201:15, remaining after = 4.

review.reason: Spec basis verified in evidence openapi.json: POST /coupons/{code}/claim says "Claim one use of a coupon. remaining never goes below zero." and declares 409 "Quota exhausted", so successes<=initial remaining is a documented invariant, not a guessed business rule. The script is self-contained (fetch against TARGET, default localhost:4100), resets state, reads remaining=5, fires remaining+10=15 concurrent claims, and asserts only the spec-derived invariant (ok>remaining || remaining<0), exiting non-zero on violation; it exits 0 on infrastructure errors, so it isn't failing for environmental reasons. Rerun output shows 201:15, 409:0 with quota 5 — a clear over-claim. The finding is not trivially unfailable: sequential behavior is stated (and uncontradicted) to return 409 at remaining=0, so a correct implementation passes. Minor inconsistency: description says final remaining=4 while the rerun shows 3 (evidence file shows 4); this is expected nondeterminism from the race and does not affect the core claim — in both cases 15 claims succeeded against quota 5 and remaining is far from 5-15=-10, so the "remaining not decremented per successful claim" point also holds. Description, script, and output agree on the reproduced defect.

title: GET /products drops the last product: total=10 but only 9 items ever listed
description:
What happens: GET /products?size=100 (and every other page size) reports total=10 but returns only 9 items; the last product in the catalogue (p10 after adding 3 products to the 7 seed products) never appears on any page. GET /products/p10 returns 200, so the product exists and is orderable — it is simply invisible in the listing. The off-by-one is stable across page sizes 3, 7 and 100 and across a fresh reset plus 3 created products, so it is not a paging-window artifact.

Expected: the union of all pages equals the full catalogue, i.e. `total` distinct products, per the /openapi.json description of GET /products: "A page of products. Every product appears on exactly one page." Here 1 of 10 products appears on zero pages.

Impact: a client that builds its catalogue by paging (the only documented way to enumerate products, since there is no single-list endpoint) can never see or order the last product; total is also inconsistent with the returned items.

Repro: `node .prelude/work/pagination-probe.mjs` — resets, creates 3 products, then walks all pages for size 3/7/100 and prints the count mismatch plus the ids that exist via GET /products/{id} but are missing from the listing.

review.reason: 预期值来自 openapi.json 对 GET /products 200 的明确描述（"Every product appears on exactly one page"）与 ProductPage.total，非自拟规则；失败非分页窗口伪影——pages=4 与 total=10 自洽（ceil(10/3)），脚本走完全部页仍只得 9 个，size=100 单页也只回 9 个；缺失的 p10 经 GET /products/{id}=200 证明确实存在，故 total 与 items 内部矛盾，任何实现都应满足该文档不变量；脚本异常时 exit(0)，因此退出码 1 不会由语法/依赖/环境问题伪造；描述、脚本与三次重跑输出完全一致。

title: POST /products accepts stock<0 and non-numeric price, returning Products that violate the documented schema
description:
What happens: POST /products accepts input that produces a response violating the documented Product schema. (1) {"name":"neg-stock","stock":-5} -> 201 {"id":"p8","price":0,"stock":-5}: the returned Product has stock=-5 although Product.stock is documented as integer with minimum 0, and NewProduct.stock is documented as integer with no explicit lower bound, so the server should reject or clamp, not emit a negative stock. (2) {"name":"bad-price","price":"not-a-number"} -> 201 {"id":"p9","price":null,"stock":0}: NewProduct.price is type number, but a string is accepted and silently coerced to null in the created Product, so the response violates Product.price (type number).

Expected: invalid input is rejected with 400 (the endpoint already declares a 400 "Invalid input" response and does return 400 for a missing/empty name), or the value is coerced to a schema-valid one. Basis: /openapi.json components.schemas.Product (price: number, stock: integer minimum 0) and NewProduct (price: number, stock: integer), plus the declared 400 response on POST /products.

Impact: a product with negative stock is permanently un-orderable (POST /orders returns 409 "insufficient stock" against it) and is served to every client as a Product that breaks their generated types; a null price breaks price arithmetic in clients. Both defects survive a reset only via creation, and neither can be fixed from the API.

Repro: `node .prelude/work/product-validation-probe.mjs` — resets, creates the two products, and asserts the returned Product obeys its documented schema.

review.reason: The claim is grounded in the project's own /openapi.json, which I verified: POST /products 201 is defined as $ref Product, where Product.stock is integer with minimum 0 and Product.price is type number; a 400 "Invalid input" response is also declared. The probe asserts only when the server returns 201 AND the body violates that response schema, so a schema-conforming implementation (e.g. returning 400, as it does for empty name) would pass — the assertion is not vacuous. The expectations (stock < 0, typeof price !== number) come from the schema, not from the observed output. The description, script and captured output are consistent: stock=-5 and price="not-a-number" both yield 201 with bodies ({"stock":-5}, {"price":null}) that cannot validate as Product. The rerun reached the assertions and exited 1 in all three runs, so failures are not script/env artifacts. The only weak point is that NewProduct.stock lacks a minimum, but the response-schema violation alone is sufficient, and the string price is additionally invalid against NewProduct.price: number. Concrete, verifiable contract violation.

title: POST /products returns 500 (and leaks internals) for any name with an emoji / astral-plane character
description:
What happens: POST /products returns HTTP 500 {"error":"internal error","detail":"slugify: unexpected surrogate pair"} for any name containing an astral-plane (non-BMP) character, e.g. "🎉", "a🎉", "Sprocket 🛒", "日本語テスト🎉 café Ω". BMP non-ASCII names work fine ("日本語テスト", "café", "Ω", "ＡＢ" all return 201), so the failure is specific to UTF-16 surrogate pairs. No product is created (total unchanged, p8 does not exist), so the request is also a hard failure for the caller.

Expected: the name is accepted (201) or rejected with 400 "Invalid input". Basis: /openapi.json NewProduct.name is documented as "Any UTF-8 text"; POST /products declares 201 Created and 400 Invalid input — 5xx is not part of the contract, and a valid UTF-8 string must not crash the handler. The blind-spot list calls out non-ASCII input and legal input must not produce 5xx.

Secondary issue in the same response: the 500 body leaks internal implementation detail ("slugify: unexpected surrogate pair"), which tells an attacker exactly which internal function runs and how it is implemented.

Repro: `node .prelude/work/emoji-name-probe.mjs` — resets, posts four astral-plane names, and fails if any returns 5xx.

review.reason: 证据自洽且可验证：脚本对 4 个 astral-plane（emoji）名称发起 POST /products，仅当返回 >=500 时退出码为 1，3 次重跑均稳定为 1，输出全为 500 且 detail 为 "slugify: unexpected surrogate pair"，与描述完全一致。预期依据来自证据中的 /openapi.json：NewProduct.name 标注 "Any UTF-8 text"，POST /products 仅声明 201/400，5xx 不属于契约；BMP 非 ASCII 名称返回 201 说明失败确为代理对相关，而非通用的名称校验。次要的"泄漏内部实现细节"也有具体可验证的响应字段支撑。脚本的 catch 分支 exit 0 是保守写法，只会漏报不会误报，且重跑无 stderr 说明请求正常执行。

title: Concurrent cancel + order on the same product creates inventory out of thin air (units not conserved)
description:
What happens: interleaving POST /orders/{id}/cancel with POST /orders against the same product does not conserve units — inventory is created. Setup: reset p1 to stock 20, place 5 sequential orders of qty 2 (stock correctly 10). Then fire 5 cancels of those orders and 5 new orders of qty 2 concurrently: all 10 succeed (200 x5, 201 x5), final stock 18, placed qty 10, cancelled qty 10. Accounting: stock(18) + placed(10) = 28 units for 20 that ever existed, i.e. 8 units materialised. Reproduced 3/3 rounds.

Expected: initialStock == finalStock + total qty of orders still in status "placed". Basis: /openapi.json POST /orders "Stock is decremented by qty" and POST /orders/{id}/cancel "Cancel an order and return its quantity to stock" — an order either holds units (placed) or has returned them (cancelled), so the sum must be invariant. Each step is correct in isolation: 5 sequential orders 20->10 and 5 cancels alone restore exactly (verified separately: 6 concurrent cancels of 6 different orders from stock 8 -> 20 exactly).

Root cause is the same non-atomic read-modify-write on the stock counter as f-001, but the observable symptom and the fix verification differ: here the counter moves in both directions and units are created rather than oversold, so a fix that only guards the 409 check in the order path would not close this. Repro: `node .prelude/work/conserve-probe.mjs`.

review.reason: The invariant is grounded in the API contract captured in the supplied openapi.json (POST /orders decrements stock by qty; POST /orders/{id}/cancel returns qty to stock; Order.status enum is placed|cancelled), not in a guessed rule. A correct implementation gives finalStock 10 + placedQty 10 = 20, so the check is not trivially satisfiable/failing. The script cannot produce a false positive from its own environment: all work is inside try/catch that exits 0 on error, and the observed numbers are self-consistent (5 sequential orders 20->10 as expected, 5x200 cancels, 5x201 orders, yet finalStock 18), which is the signature of a lost update on the stock counter where cancel's +2 writes overwrite order's -2 writes. Description, script and 3/3 run output agree, and the service notes independently document the stock counter as a non-atomic read-modify-write with cancels being correct in isolation — consistent with the claimed root cause and with why this differs from f-001 (units created, not oversold) and why a 409-only guard would not close it.
